title: The eight-legged problem solver
text: Few creatures {{1}} been studied as eagerly as the octopus. It has no bones, {{2}} means it can escape {{3}} almost any aquarium that is not carefully sealed. Its eight arms taste, grip and react independently of {{4}} other, and in laboratory mazes it solves problems faster {{5}} many vertebrates do. The animal {{6}} seems to play, directing jets of water at lamp bulbs out of apparent curiosity, and keepers report individual temperaments as marked as a dog's. Such behaviour {{7}} once dismissed as simple reflex, but biologists now speak of distributed intelligence, with two thirds of an octopus's neurons located in the arms rather than the brain. There is still {{8}} single accepted definition of what intelligence means in a creature so distant from us, which is perhaps why the octopus keeps surprising the people who study it.

gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a plural subject: 'few creatures have been studied'.
Non-defining relative clause after the comma; only 'which' is possible.
'Escape from' — from marks the place being left behind.
'Each other' is the reciprocal pronoun for a mutual action.
A comparative adjective ('faster') requires 'than' before the second element.

gaps.hint: reflexive: the animal ___ seems to play
gaps.explanation: Emphatic reflexive: 'the animal itself' stresses the whole creature.

gaps.hint: passive auxiliary: such behaviour ___ once dismissed
gaps.explanation: Past passive with a singular subject: the behaviour was dismissed.
'No' negates the noun directly; 'not' cannot precede 'single accepted definition'.
